title: Bystander Responses to Intimate Partner Violence in Heterosexual and Same-Sex Relationships: The Role of Perpetrator Gender and Relationship Sexual Orientation
abstract: Although prior research has identified factors associated with bystander willingness to intervene in intimate partner violence (IPV), whether responses differ across heterosexual and same-sex relationships remains underexplored. Using a vignette design with 182 college students, this study examined whether perpetrator gender and relationship sexual orientation influenced awareness of violence, post-situation informal intervention, and willingness to report the incident to police. A significant perpetrator gender × relationship sexual orientation interaction emerged for police reporting. The interaction showed a crossover pattern: descriptively, reporting willingness was greater for male than female perpetrators in heterosexual vignettes, whereas the pattern reversed in same-sex vignettes. However, neither within-context perpetrator-gender comparison reached statistical significance in follow-up simple-effects analyses, indicating that the interaction should be interpreted cautiously.
